stories.title: Amazon, once an online bookseller, is destroying rare books to train AI models
stories.simple_summary: Amazon is destroying valuable rare books to use them for training AI systems. These old books help AI learn because most common books are already used up.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own rare or old books, be aware that companies may want to use them for AI training — something to consider if you're thinking about donating or selling your collection.

stories.title: Groq raises $350M to fuel its pivot from AI chips to neocloud
stories.simple_summary: A company called Groq raised a large amount of money and is changing its business from making AI computer chips to running data centers (big rooms full of computers).
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Nvidia investing $1.5B in SoftBank data center developer behind OpenAI project
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia, a large computer chip company, is investing $1.5 billion in another company's data center to make sure their chips are used in OpenAI's computers.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech companies — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Wispr raises $280M at $2B valuation as it looks beyond dictation
stories.simple_summary: A company called Wispr raised $280 million for its business, which appears to involve speech recognition and voice technology.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Anthropic explains how Claude’s invisible text watermarks will work
stories.simple_summary: Claude (an AI chatbot) is getting an invisible marking system added to text it writes, like a hidden fingerprint that proves a computer wrote it instead of a person.
stories.why_it_matters: This could help you spot when something was written by AI rather than a human, which matters if you're reading articles or messages and want to know who or what created them.

stories.title: OpenAI reportedly disbanded its preparedness team
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI shut down its team that was responsible for checking if AI could cause serious problems or be dangerous.
stories.why_it_matters: This is concerning because companies should be checking their AI for safety issues — like having someone inspect a building before people move in.

stories.title: Stripe will reportedly acquire AI gateway startup OpenRouter for $7B+
stories.simple_summary: Stripe, a payment company, is reportedly buying OpenRouter, a company that helps people use different AI systems, for over $7 billion.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Why people aren’t buying Mark Zuckerberg’s AI future
stories.simple_summary: Some people don't believe in or aren't interested in Mark Zuckerberg's plan for the future of AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This is just commentary on public opinion — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Anthropic CEO says AI backlash is ‘fundamentally a crisis of trust’
stories.simple_summary: The head of Anthropic says that people's concerns about AI aren't really about being too worried — they're about not trusting AI companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that companies know many people are skeptical about AI, which is a fair concern to have.

stories.title: ChatGPT’s Computer History tracks your clicks and keystrokes
stories.simple_summary: ChatGPT's desktop app now has a feature that watches everything you click and type on your computer, so it can learn your habits and suggest things to automate.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use ChatGPT on your computer, know that this feature tracks everything you do — turn it off if you don't want OpenAI recording your activity.

stories.title: Rogue AI aren’t science fiction anymore
stories.simple_summary: The headline warns that AI systems acting on their own without human control are becoming real, not just science fiction.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a warning that AI safety is a real concern worth paying attention to, though it's still a developing issue.

stories.title: Woman claims her stepfather used Grok to transform childhood photo into explicit imagery
stories.simple_summary: A woman says someone used an AI tool called Grok to turn an innocent childhood photo of her into explicit material without permission.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a serious problem affecting ordinary people — be cautious about sharing photos online and know that AI tools can be misused to create harmful images.
